by: Two research agents (the class list, and the market and finance signals), then a check of each record before the commit.
method: The class research read lists of hazards, alert codes and the categories of risk products, then found sources for each class. The finance research did the same for prediction markets and finance signals. The check made each decision a calculation, opened each evidence link of the planned sources, and checked the facts that change a decision.

notes: The UNDRR-ISC HIPs 2025 list was read from the IFRC Monty taxonomy page, which copies the full 2025 hazard list with codes (281 hazards, 8 types). The UNDRR and IRDR PDF reports were not opened.

Reference lists not opened in round 1: the WEF Global Risks Report 2026 appendix (HTTP 403 on both domains), the Everbridge risk intelligence category guide (login), the UNDRR/ISC HIPs PDFs (the 2025 list was read through the IFRC Monty page), the full category lists of Dataminr, Factal, Crisis24 and Samdesk (only marketing pages), the Cloudflare outage center page, IsDown, the StatusGator API page, IODA documentation (empty page), Downdetector (blocked) and the ThousandEyes outage map (403).

Many government pages refused the fetch tool or rendered only a title (NVD, State Department, FCC, PHMSA, NAVCEN, NGA MSI, WZDx, NHTSA datasets, Federal Register bot check). Round 2 needs a browser-based check of these sources before a decision.
ECDC replaced the weekly Communicable Disease Threats Report with daily public health event updates in October 2026 (from the ECDC page).
The CDC NWSS SARS-CoV-2 dataset on data.cdc.gov (2ew6-ywp6) is archived since 12 September 2025. Current NWSS datasets were not found.
openFDA says its enforcement data must not be used to issue public alerts, and recall status is not updated after classification. Recall alerts need the press-release channels of each agency.

Weather-only coverage: the NWS API relays some non-weather IPAWS codes (CAE, BLU, LEW, SPW, EVI, CDW, CEM, LAE, TOE, HMW, RHW, NUW), so a weather system that reads all NWS event types gets part of the safety and cbrne classes, but only when an authority uses IPAWS and the relay.
This file records data sources and their properties only. It is not investment advice.

Pages that I could not read: Metaculus track record (HTTP 403), goodjudgment.com (403), SSRN abstract 5331995 (403), developer.betfair.com (403, so Betfair is not covered), investor.gov (403), kalshi.com/developer-agreement (429; the S3 PDF of v1.1 was read instead), the PredictIt help article (login redirect), the PredictIt terms (script-rendered), the Cboe Use of Content page (404 at the URL tried), otce.finra.org (script-rendered), the FINRA investor insights RSS path (404), and the Treasury Fiscal Data API call (no connection).

Region limits on reading data: the Binance API returned HTTP 451 to a plain read from the research location. Polymarket blocks order placement by region, not reading. Kalshi limits API data use by its agreement, not by region. Insight Prediction forbids trading from the US.
SEC fair access needs a declared User-Agent with an organization and a contact email. The system must use a project contact, never a person.

Unverified (search results only, pages not opened or empty): Bernile, Hu and Tang 2016 FOMC lockup findings and profit estimates of $4.5M to $210.5M; the Kurov et al. sample period 2008 to 2014; the Nobel 2025 Machado odds move from 3.6% to over 70%; reports that 57% of flagged Polymarket wallets on Iran-related markets were made less than 24 hours before their trades, with about $1M made before the February strikes and about $600k before the April 7 ceasefire; Ng, Peng, Tao and Zhou (SSRN 5331995) that Polymarket led Kalshi in price discovery in 2024; the Prediction Hunt free tier of 1,000 requests a month; a Downdetector enterprise price from $2,083 a month (StatusGator, a competitor) and a new Downdetector Pro plan with API access (ISPreview, 2026-09).

Venues seen only in third-party docs or search results, not given source records: Hyperliquid HIP-4 outcome markets (POST https://api.hyperliquid.xyz/info with type outcomeMeta; launched 2026-05-02, mostly BTC binaries), ForecastEx (needs an IBKR market-data subscription), and the aggregators FinFeedAPI, Tatum, PolyRouter, MarketMaster, SportsGameOdds and Codex. Metaforecast appears shut down: metaforecast.org redirects to quantifieduncertainty.org, which only links back.

Not researched in round 1: Betfair, Crypto.com and Robinhood event contracts, Polymarket US, INFER, Hypermind, brier.fyi or calibration.city, credit rating agencies, FINRA OTC halts in detail, chain halts other than Solana, and an official Visa or Mastercard network status page (a search found none).

Calibration found: Polymarket Brier 0.0605 (self-published); Manifold Brier 0.17425 (self-published, play money); Kalshi blog 2026-08-20 with values only in charts; the Fed FEDS 2026-010 paper on Kalshi macro markets (as summarized by natlawreview.com). The UT Austin Kalshi weather post describes a method but gives no numbers in its text.

Lead-time summary: futures drift about 30 minutes before some US macro releases; event-market leaks in the cited cases show up from hours to about half a day ahead; public shocks (a debate, an assassination attempt) show no rise before the event. So market signals add minutes to hours of lead only for some leaked or scheduled events.

Kalshi has the best-documented calibration for US macro and weather events, but its Developer Agreement v1.1 limits API use to a member's own trading. Written permission from Kalshi is the only route to use it.

Self-reported status pages (Atlassian Statuspage JSON at /api/v2/status.json) worked with no auth for Coinbase, Kraken, Gemini, Circle, Solana, Square, Plaid, Chime, Robinhood and Visa Acceptance Solutions on 2026-11-15. Stripe has no such endpoint (404) and PayPal redirects.
The research used the auth value unknown for 15 sources: no page that it opened said how access works. A source with this value is later until a round finds the auth.
The research did not find the IPAWS public feed: its page returned 404. The adapter source-ipaws of this repository reads the feed, so the check added it as ipaws-open.

The check made the decision a calculation (planBlock). A source is planned only when its auth is none, key or account, its cost is free or free-tier, and its terms do not forbid automated reading. A page source also needs terms that let automated reading. This rule moved 25 sources to later: fed-fomc-calendar (a page source needs terms that let automated reading), freddie-mac-pmms (a page source needs terms that let automated reading), frbservices-status (a page source needs terms that let automated reading), nasdaq-system-status (a page source needs terms that let automated reading), nyse-holidays-page (the terms forbid automated reading), census-econ-calendar (a page source needs terms that let automated reading), ofac-recent-actions (a page source needs terms that let automated reading), usgs-hans-api (the auth is unknown), swpc-email (the cost is unknown), nwps-api (the auth is unknown), nws-heatrisk (a page source needs terms that let automated reading), openaq-api (the cost is unknown), epa-cyan-api (the auth is unknown), ecdc-threats (a page source needs terms that let automated reading), fda-core-investigations (a page source needs terms that let automated reading), wastewaterscan (a page source needs terms that let automated reading), aphis-hpai (a page source needs terms that let automated reading), woah-wahis (a page source needs terms that let automated reading), github-advisories-api (the auth is unknown), ioda-api (the auth is unknown), odin-ornl (a page source needs terms that let automated reading), usps-service-alerts (a page source needs terms that let automated reading), acled-api (the cost is unknown), gtfs-rt-alerts (the auth is unknown), eurdep (a page source needs terms that let automated reading).
The check took the class infra.power.grid-emergency off eia-api: EIA gives the demand of the grid, not the notices of the grid operators.

An adopted or planned source needs evidence: a page that a round opened. Three planned sources had none. The check opened the AWS status feed and one answer of the NVD API. The FSIS pages returned 403, so fsis-recall-api is later.
The check added the three sources that adapters of this repository read (nws-alerts-api, ipaws-open, iem-vtec), and eagle-i-history.

The check opened the FEMA fact sheet of the IPAWS feed: it asks each provider for a Memorandum of Agreement. It is not clear that a personal receiver needs one. Until that is clear, the terms of ipaws-open are unclear, and ipaws-open has a risk. The gate does not count a source with a risk, so 9 classes name the risk in their gap.
The research did not record the subject ids of each source. Only the adopted sources and eagle-i-history have them. A value of null means not researched.
The class ids took the codes of TAXONOMY of the core, so the system has one id for each kind. The core holds the label and the summary of each class.
14 class ids changed to the core code of the same meaning. Three changes merged two classes: cbrne.hazardous-materials, infra.payments.outage and infra.fuel.shortage.
met.surf-and-rip-current split into met.surf, met.rip-current and met.beach-hazards, the three NWS products. 13 classes were added for core codes that no class reached.
After the change the atlas has 200 classes. The gate needs a class at each code of the taxonomy, its ancestor or its descendant.
The measures of round 1 at the merge of PR 115: 188 classes, 128 gaps and an adopted cover of 16. After the change of the ids: 200 classes, 131 gaps and an adopted cover of 24.
The adopted cover counts the classes with 2 or more adopted sources with no risk. Only 3 sources are adopted, so the gap count shows the plans and the adopted cover shows the outcome.
Round 1 searched 39 queries and 58 lists. Round 2 starts with the sources that refused the fetch tool, the terms that are unclear, and the subject ids.

studies.title: Kurov, Sancetta, Strasser and Wolfe, 'Price Drift before U.S. Macroeconomic News: Private Information about Public Announcements?', JFQA 2019
studies.finding: Stock index and Treasury futures start to move in the right direction about 30 minutes before 9 of 20 market-moving US releases; the drift is about 40% of the total price move.

studies.title: Bernile, Hu and Tang, 'Can information be locked up? Informed trading ahead of macro-news announcements', JFE 2016
studies.finding: E-mini S&P 500 order imbalance during the FOMC lockup points to the coming surprise; no such effect for payrolls, PPI or GDP.

studies.title: Polgreen, Nelson and Neumann, 'Use of prediction markets to forecast infectious disease activity', Clinical Infectious Diseases 2007 (CIDRAP summary)
studies.finding: An Iowa flu market forecast the next week's activity level correctly 50% of the time against 36% for historical averages; the authors claimed 2 to 4 weeks of lead on season start and peak.

studies.title: Tsang and Yang, Polymarket 2024 election shocks at 5-minute resolution (arXiv 2603.03152)
studies.finding: The debate and the assassination attempt each moved Trump YES by about 11 cents at peak with no clear rise before; Harris YES rose well before the July 21 dropout.

studies.title: Nobel Peace Prize 2025 Polymarket trades (news reports)
studies.finding: Machado's odds began to spike on the evening before the 11:00 Oslo announcement, about half a day ahead; Norwegian officials investigated a possible leak.

studies.title: Diercks, Katz and Wright, 'Kalshi and the Rise of Macro Markets', FEDS 2026-010
studies.finding: No lead time given; the modal fed funds outcome was right on the eve of each FOMC meeting since 2022, and odds moved within days on Fed speeches and the jobs report (per natlawreview.com).
